items.title: Ajudar a defender contra o envenenamento de memória no Amazon Bedrock AgentCore com validação de escrita em várias camadas
items.summary: A Amazon detalhou como proteger o Amazon Bedrock AgentCore contra o envenenamento de memória, uma forma de injeção indireta de prompts onde atacantes inserem instruções maliciosas na memória de longo prazo de um agente de IA. Para mitigar este risco, a solução propõe combinar controlos nativos já existentes, como políticas IAM, o Cedar e a API ApplyGuardrail, com um novo sinal de desvio semântico baseado em embeddings. Esta abordagem em profundidade ajuda a detetar conteúdos anómalos ou ofuscados sem exigir alterações diretas ao código do agente.
points: O quê: Mitigação de envenenamento de memória e injeção de prompts em IA.
Como: Combinação de controlos AWS IAM, Cedar, Guardrails e validação semântica.
Impacto: Prevenção de comportamentos maliciosos persistentes em agentes de IA.
Quem: Administradores e programadores que utilizam o Amazon Bedrock.
items.title_original: Help defend against memory poisoning in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with multi-layer write validation
items.why: Protege os agentes de IA contra manipulações persistentes que podem comprometer o seu comportamento futuro.
items.todo: Implemente uma estratégia de defesa em profundidade combinando validação de escrita, políticas de acesso restritas e monitorização semântica.

items.title: Google lança novos TPUs para otimizar tarefas de agentes de IA e melhorar segurança
items.summary: O Google anunciou o lançamento dos novos chips de inteligência artificial TPU 8tx e TPU 8i Max, focados em melhorar o desempenho e a segurança de agentes autônomos no setor produtivo. O modelo TPU 8tx integra proteções diretamente na camada de hardware para isolar dados sensíveis e pesos de modelos, permitindo também o ajuste fino com dados privados. Por sua vez, o TPU 8i Max foi concebido para eliminar gargalos de memória e duplicar o poder computacional para lidar com dezenas de agentes em simultâneo.
points: O quê: Lançamento dos novos processadores TPU 8tx e TPU 8i Max pelo Google.
Como: Integração de segurança por hardware e aumento de capacidade de memória e computação.
Impacto: Maior proteção de dados sensíveis e melhor desempenho para agentes de IA autónomos.
Quem: Empresas e governos que treinam modelos de IA avançados.
items.why: Oferece infraestrutura com segurança integrada por hardware para cargas de trabalho de IA corporativa altamente reguladas.
items.todo: Considere avaliar aceleradores de IA com isolamento de dados por hardware para proteger cargas de trabalho sensíveis.

items.title: França culpa o Irão por ciberataques a frigoríficos e diz que alguns causaram incêndios
items.summary: As autoridades francesas atribuíram um conjunto de ciberataques ocorridos em outubro a um grupo ligado ao Irão, especificamente à unidade Shahid Kaveh dos Guardas da Revolução Islâmica. A operação afetou sistemas de refrigeração em mais de 700 supermercados e locais de retalho, provocando perdas alimentares e pelo menos 15 incêndios. O incidente destaca o risco crescente de ataques informáticos direcionados a controladores industriais e infraestruturas físicas.
points: O quê: Ciberataques a sistemas de refrigeração em supermercados franceses.
Quem: Atribuídos à unidade cibernética iraniana Shahid Kaveh.
Como: Interrupção remota de controladores industriais e sistemas de frio.
Impacto: Perda de alimentos e pelo menos 15 incêndios em espaços comerciais.
items.title_original: France blames Iran for fridge cyberattacks, says some caused fires
items.why: Revela como ciberataques a sistemas industriais podem causar danos físicos graves no mundo real, incluindo incêndios.
items.todo: Refforce a segurança e a segmentação de rede em sistemas de controlo industrial e dispositivos IoT comerciais.

items.title: França culpa hackers iranianos por ataques a supermercados que desencadearam incêndios
items.summary: O governo de França responsabilizou hackers apoiados pelo Estado iraniano pelos ciberataques registados em outubro contra sistemas de refrigeração em mais de 700 superfícies comerciais. Os incidentes perturbaram o funcionamento de locais de retalho, resultaram na perda de produtos alimentares e causaram diretamente pelo menos 15 incêndios. Esta é a primeira atribuição oficial efetuada pelas autoridades francesas desde que os ataques ocorreram.
points: O quê: Ciberataques contra sistemas de frio em mais de 700 locais de retalho.
Quem: Hackers patrocinados pelo Estado iraniano.
Impacto: Destruição de alimentos e deflagração de pelo menos 15 incêndios.
Como: Invasão e perturbação remota de sistemas de refrigeração.
items.title_original: France blames Iranian hackers for supermarket attacks that sparked fires
items.why: Sublinha a vulnerabilidade de infraestruturas comerciais essenciais a ataques estatais com impacto físico destrutivo.
items.todo: Garanta a monitorização contínua e o isolamento de redes de refrigeração e automação comercial.

items.title: Incidente de cibersegurança afeta dispositivos e sistemas do campus de Vanderbilt
items.summary: A Universidade Vanderbilt emitiu um alerta a informar os estudantes e funcionários sobre a ocorrência de um ciberataque. O incidente poderá ter comprometido vários dispositivos e sistemas ligados à rede do campus. As equipas de segurança estão a avaliar a extensão da ocorrência para mitigar possíveis danos.
points: O quê: Incidente de cibersegurança numa instituição de ensino superior.
Quem: Universidade Vanderbilt e respetivos utilizadores (estudantes e funcionários).
Impacto: Potencial compromisso de dispositivos e sistemas do campus.
Como: Ataque informático sob investigação.
items.title_original: Vanderbilt cybersecurity incident impacting campus devices and systems
items.why: Demonstra que instituições académicas continuam a ser alvos frequentes de incidentes de cibersegurança.
items.todo: Mantenha os dispositivos afetados isolados da rede institucional até que as autoridades de TI confirmem a sua segurança.

items.title: Atacantes procuram webshells SAP Netweaver
items.summary: Dados recolhidos através de sistemas de 'honeypot' detetaram novas tentativas de exploração e sondagem direcionadas a vulnerabilidades em ambientes SAP Netweaver. Os atacantes surgiram à procura de webshells existentes ou a tentar instalar novos pontos de acesso para comprometer os servidores afetados. Este tipo de atividade demonstra a procura constante por superfícies de ataque expostas em software empresarial.
points: O quê: Tentativas de exploração e procura de webshells SAP Netweaver.
Como: Deteção de URLs maliciosos através de dados de honeypots.
Impacto: Risco de acesso não autorizado a sistemas empresariais SAP.
Quem: Atacantes não especificados à procura de vulnerabilidades.
items.title_original: Attackers Searching for SAP Netweaver Webshells, (Mon, Nov 9th)
items.why: Evidencia a exploração automatizada e contínua de plataformas corporativas por parte de cibercriminosos.
items.todo: Aplique imediatamente patches de segurança em sistemas SAP e verifique a existência de webshells ou acessos anómalos.

items.title: Atacantes exploram falha na 'Festa de Escritório' do Claude para executar código malicioso no Linux
items.summary: Investigadores descobriram que atacantes podem tirar partido de uma vulnerabilidade na ferramenta de processamento de documentos do assistente de IA Claude. O vetor de ataque envolve a criação de um ficheiro temporário que o assistente acede e executa automaticamente na máquina do utilizador. Esta falha permite comprometer sistemas operativos Linux através da execução de código não autorizado.
points: O quê: Exploração de falha na ferramenta de documentos do Claude.
Como: Criação de um ficheiro temporário executado pelo assistente de IA.
Impacto: Execução de código malicioso em máquinas com Linux.
Quem: Atacantes que exploram a ferramenta de processamento da Anthropic.
items.title_original: Attackers Crash Claude's 'Office Party' Flaw to Run Malicious Code on Linux
items.why: Mostra como vulnerabilidades em ferramentas de IA assistivas podem ser transformadas em vetores de execução remota de código.
items.todo: Atualize ferramentas de IA e assistentes de desenvolvimento para as versões mais recentes corrigidas.

items.title: Hackers exploram acesso AWS confiável da Qubole para invadir contas de clientes e roubar dados
items.summary: Entre 14 e 26 de outubro, atacantes conseguiram violar contas na AWS pertencentes a vários clientes da plataforma de dados Qubole. O intruso utilizou credenciais de uma conta AWS que a própria Qubole utilizava para interagir com os ambientes dos clientes, embora a forma como obteve esses dados não tenha sido revelada. O ataque resultou no roubo de credenciais armazenadas e de dados confidenciais.
points: O quê: Violação de contas AWS de clientes da Qubole.
Como: Utilização de credenciais de acesso privilegiado da plataforma Qubole.
Impacto: Roubo de dados e segredos armazenados na cloud.
Quem: Atacantes desconhecidos que visaram clientes da Qubole.
items.title_original: Hackers Exploit Qubole's Trusted AWS Access to Breach Customer Accounts and Steal Data
items.why: Ilustra os riscos de segurança associados a acessos de terceiros e cadeias de fornecimento na cloud.
items.todo: Audite regularmente as permissões de acesso atribuídas a fornecedores terceiros e implemente o princípio do privilégio mínimo.

items.title: Empresa russa de cloud Beget reconstrói infraestrutura do zero após ataque com wiper
items.summary: A empresa russa de serviços cloud Beget foi obrigada a reconstruir toda a sua infraestrutura tecnológica a partir do zero na sequência de um ciberataque destrutivo. Os atacantes utilizaram malware do tipo 'data wiper' com o objetivo de apagar dados e paralisar os servidores da organização. A empresa teve de efetuar um restablecimento completo dos seus sistemas.
points: O quê: Ataque com malware destruidor de dados (wiper) a fornecedor de cloud.
Quem: Empresa de alojamento cloud Beget.
Impacto: Destruição total de dados e necessidade de reconstrução da infraestrutura.
Como: Infeção por ransomware/wiper direcionado a servidores.
items.title_original: Russian cloud firm Beget rebuilds from scratch after data wiper attack
items.why: Demonstra a capacidade devastadora de ataques com wipers capazes de destruir infraestruturas cloud inteiras.
items.todo: Mantenha cópias de segurança (backups) imutáveis e isoladas da rede principal para garantir a recuperabilidade.

items.title: Hackers comprometem bee-js da Ethersphere e o Swarm Desktop para distribuir malware rouba-carteiras
items.summary: Atacantes comprometeram os mecanismos de automação de lançamento do projeto Ethersphere para publicar versões maliciosas de duas ferramentas da rede de armazenamento descentralizado Swarm (o bee-js 13.3.0 e o Swarm Desktop 0.56.2). As versões adulteradas executam código para roubar chaves de carteiras de criptomoedas e respetivas passwords guardadas no nó, além de instalarem uma backdoor no sistema.
points: O quê: Distribuição de versões maliciosas de bee-js e Swarm Desktop.
Como: Compromisso da automação de lançamentos do projeto Ethersphere.
Impacto: Roubo de chaves de carteiras digitais e instalação de backdoors.
Quem: Atacantes que visaram utilizadores da rede Swarm.
items.title_original: Hackers Compromise Ethersphere's bee-js and Swarm Desktop to Deliver Wallet-Stealing Malware
items.why: Evidencia o perigo de ataques à cadeia de fornecimento de software e gestão de dependências em projetos descentralizados.
items.todo: Verifique assinaturas e hashes de pacotes de software antes de os instalar ou atualizar em ambientes de produção.

items.title: Investigadores exploram aplicações Android de construtores automóveis para desbloquear carros e buzinar remotamente
items.summary: Investigadores de cibersegurança descobriram falhas em aplicações Android de dois grandes construtores automóveis, permitindo o controlo remoto de veículos na Austrália e nos Estados Unidos. O ataque aproveitou-se de vulnerabilidades na plataforma de identidade ForgeRock, incluindo credenciais de administrador predefinidas ou hardcoded e falhas de travessia de diretórios (path traversal) para contornar defesas WAF. Com estes acessos, conseguiram emitir comandos para abrir portas, acender luzes e acionar buzinas.
points: O quê: Exploração de falhas em apps Android de marcas automóveis.
Quem: Investigadores Shubham Shah e Sam Curry.
Como: Abuso de falhas na plataforma ForgeRock, credenciais por defeito e path traversal.
Impacto: Acesso remoto não autorizado a veículos para executar comandos físicos.
items.title_original: Researchers pwn automakers’ Android apps to remotely unlock cars, honk horns
items.why: Revela graves falhas de autenticação e gestão de APIs em aplicações móveis ligadas a veículos conectados.
items.todo: Elimine credenciais predefinidas ou de testes em ambientes de produção e aplique validação rigorosa de inputs em APIs.

items.title: Claude Code expõe acidentalmente segredos por todo o GitHub
items.summary: Investigadores de segurança da Apiiro descobriram que a ferramenta Claude Code tem estado a divulgar inadvertidamente milhares de segredos confidenciais em repositórios públicos no GitHub. A fuga ocorre devido à forma como o assistente gere os ficheiros de configuração locais, gravando comandos aprovados que contêm dados sensíveis como palavras-passe de bases de dados e tokens de API. Embora estes ficheiros devessem ser ignorados por predefinição, a inclusão de regras parciais tem levado utilizadores a partilhá-los publicamente por lapso.
points: O quê: Fuga massiva de dados sensíveis em repositórios públicos do GitHub.
Quem: Investigadores da Apiiro e utilizadores da ferramenta Claude Code.
Como: Gravação acidental de comandos com credenciais em ficheiros de configuração locais.
Impacto: Exposição pública de palavras-passe, tokens de API e dados de acesso.
items.title_original: Claude Code is accidentally exposing secrets all over GitHub
items.why: Alerta para o risco de ferramentas de automação exporem credenciais sensíveis através de ficheiros de configuração locais.
items.todo: Configure corretamente os ficheiros .gitignore e audite repositórios públicos para garantir que não partilha dados confidenciais.

items.raw: Overview Multiple vulnerabilities in the FrodoBots EarthRover Mini+ firmware (version 6.2.4_6.2.5_0.614.0) may allow remote code execution, unauthorized access to onboard sensors, disclosure of sensitive information, and full compromise of affected devices. Exploitation may enable an attacker to remotely control the rover, access audiovisual streams, or pivot into the user’s network. Description The FrodoBots EarthRover Mini+ is a compact, internet‑connected mobile robot used in educational and consumer environments. The device includes a camera, microphone, motor controllers, and multiple onboard services. Multiple vulnerabilities in the EarthRover Mini+ firmware (version 6.2.4_6.2.5_0.614.0) can allow remote code execution, unauthorized access to onboard sensors, exposure of sensitive data, and complete device compromise. An attacker could potentially take remote control of the rover, access its audio and video streams, or use it to gain a foothold in its network. CVE-2026-121685 : The firmware contains several sets of hard-coded, fleet‑wide credentials, including BasicAuth credentials for an Agora token service, AWS IAM (Amazon Web Services Identity and Access Management) access keys, Amazon Web Services Internet of Things Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (AWS IoT MQTT) credentials, and a Slack incoming webhook URL. Agora Token Service is an open source server that generates secure, time‑limited authentication tokens for use with Agora.io’s RTC (Real‑Time Communication) and RTM (Real‑Time Messaging) services. A Slack incoming webhook URL is a unique endpoint that lets external systems send messages into a Slack channel without the need for a full Slack application. These are embedded directly in frodobot.bin and are accessible through static analysis of the publicly downloadable firmware or from any device. Extraction requires no special privileges. CVE-2026-121686 : Unauthenticated remote command execution is allowed via Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT). A firmware method accepts arbitrary shell commands delivered via Amazon Web Services Internet of Things Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (AWS IoT MQTT) messages and executes them as root. Access is gated only by shared Internet of Things (IoT) credentials, with no per‑device authentication, enabling remote code execution (RCE) as root across the fleet. items.raw: For the latest discoveries in cyber research for the week of 9th November, please download our Threat Intelligence Bulletin. TOP ATTACKS AND BREACHES Queens Public Library, a New York City public library system serving approximately 2.3 million residents, was struck by a ransomware attack that encrypted its systems. The incident disrupted public computers, Wi-Fi, checkout equipment, digital media services, and its mobile application, while all 66 branches remained open. Russian web hosting provider Beget sustained a destructive cyberattack on November 1 that wiped data across its cloud infrastructure and disrupted hundreds of websites. The attack affected businesses and public services, with more than 1,000 servers requiring manual inspection before restoration. Some backup data was reportedly destroyed. OPSSHIELD, developer of the Linux security tool cPGuard, disclosed a supply-chain attack after compromised credentials enabled attackers to distribute malicious updates on November 2. Approximately 2,950 customer servers executed the malicious script, which installed a backdoor and collected password hashes, credentials, and sensitive server files. Ukraine’s Air Alert app, an emergency notification service used by millions, was compromised by attackers who distributed false radiation, chemical-threat, and military alerts to Kyiv residents. Developers temporarily suspended notifications. A separate attack affected Russia’s emergency alert application, although both countries reported that their core warning systems remained operational. AI THREATS Check Point Research documented cybercriminals using ARTEX, an AI-powered framework that autonomously discovers and exploits vulnerable systems. Researchers identified 1,608 live, publicly accessible instances. Observed campaigns obtained more than 300 iOS signing certificates and harvested approximately 190,000 gaming credentials, including around 6,000 active accounts. Check Point Research identified Haiou, a jailbreak bundle targeting OpenAI Codex that weakens safeguards and modifies agent instructions to promote an external AI gateway. The package also installs security-related capabilities and appeared on infrastructure associated with cybercrime tools, although researchers did not establish that its developers intended criminal use. items.title: Simplify cross-partition access with AWS IAM outbound identity federation
items.summary: You can now use tokens from AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) outbound federation to assume roles in other Amazon Web Services (AWS) partitions. When your workloads run across AWS partitions such as Commercial, China, GovCloud (US), and European Sovereign Cloud, a workload in one partition might need to access resources or communicate with AWS […]
items.raw: You can now use tokens from AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) outbound federation to assume roles in other Amazon Web Services (AWS) partitions. When your workloads run across AWS partitions such as Commercial, China, GovCloud (US), and European Sovereign Cloud, a workload in one partition might need to access resources or communicate with AWS services in another partition. AWS partitions are hard isolation boundaries with independent instances of AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM), so a credential issued in one partition isn’t valid in another. As a result, direct role assumption with sts:AssumeRole doesn’t work across partition boundaries and resource policies can’t reference principals that exist in another partition. AWS IAM outbound identity federation already lets your workloads obtain a short-lived, AWS signed JSON Web Token (JWT) and use it to authenticate to external services. Today, we’re extending it with cross-partition support. Your workloads can now use that same mechanism to federate into another AWS partition. A workload in one partition obtains a short-lived JWT using sts:GetWebIdentityToken and exchanges it for temporary credentials in another partition using sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity with no long-term credentials to store or rotate. This post walks through configuring cross-partition identity federation using Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) data access as an example, but the same steps apply to any cross-partition API call. Important: If your workload requires cross-partition access, consult your compliance team to make sure that your implementation aligns with your regulatory or compliance obligations. A non-exhaustive list of examples are FedRAMP, ITAR, DoD CC SRG, GDPR, and others. Why use IAM outbound identity federation for cross-partition access? IAM outbound identity federation provides several benefits, including: Carry origin identity into authorization decisions – The destination trust policy can condition on the source identity’s context, its AWS account, organization ID ( org_id ), source AWS Region, and principal, so you authorize based on who and where the request originated, not only that a token is valid. Cross-partition audit trail – AWS CloudTrail events in the destination Region include the source principal Amazon Resource Name (ARN), source Region, and a token ID that correlates back to the source Region’s GetWebIdentityToken CloudTrail event. items.title: Microsoft's Azure Linux gets 470-plus security fixes in one almighty patching session
items.summary: A mountain of CVEs, a certificate cleanup, and yet more work for Microsoft's patching teams
items.raw: Microsoft has unleashed a whopper of an update for Azure Linux, packing more than 470 CVE fixes into a single release as the software industry's ever-growing pile of vulnerabilities shows little sign of shrinking. Over the weekend, Microsoft rolled out Azure Linux 3.0.2022 with fixes covering everything from the Linux kernel to open source packages and container software. The changelog runs to hundreds of entries, so anyone planning to read the whole thing might want to put the kettle on. Microsoft's release notes contain more than 470 CVE references, although some vulnerabilities appear multiple times because they affect different packages. So that's not necessarily 470 separate security holes, but it's still an impressive amount of patching for one release. The fixes span OpenSSL, curl, Kubernetes, Docker, QEMU, and a lengthy list of other packages that underpin modern Linux environments. The generic Linux kernel has been updated to version 6.6.161.1. There's also been some housekeeping following the eMudhra certificate incident, tracked as CVE-2026-114406. Microsoft has removed or distrusted root certificates that could validate compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates, while adding checks in Python and Go to reject the affected certificates. It has also preserved SSL.com TLS trust where required, presumably to avoid fixing one certificate headache by creating another. Container infrastructure gets plenty of attention, too, with fixes spanning KubeVirt, containerd, Docker Compose, and other components used to keep cloud workloads running. Several CVEs crop up repeatedly across these packages, helping explain the eye-watering number of entries in the changelog. The release includes less security-focused changes too, including new Dockerfiles, an OpenVMM patch for confidential computing support, fixes for systemd hangs, and adjustments to GRUB Secure Boot metadata. The hefty release comes amid an AI-fueled surge in vulnerability discovery that has left developers struggling to keep up with the resulting patch workload. As The Register reported earlier today, Linux creator Linus Torvalds reckons there may finally be signs that the flood is easing, at least in some corners of the kernel. Torvalds said fixes are now arriving faster than new bug reports in the kernel's eBPF subsystem, although he noted that most other areas haven't reached that point. items.title: VU#385711: PrestaShop Performance Debug Configuration Contains a PHP Code Injection Vulnerability
items.summary: Overview PrestaShop's back-office Performance > Debug mode functionality contains a PHP code injection vulnerability. An authenticated attacker with permission to modify debug-mode configuration can submit crafted cookie configuration values that are written into an executable PHP configuration file. Successful exploitation could allow arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the PHP process. Description PrestaShop is an open-source e-commerce platform for creating and managing online stores. Its back-office Performance configuration includes a Debug mode for developers, which is enable
items.raw: Overview PrestaShop's back-office Performance > Debug mode functionality contains a PHP code injection vulnerability. An authenticated attacker with permission to modify debug-mode configuration can submit crafted cookie configuration values that are written into an executable PHP configuration file. Successful exploitation could allow arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the PHP process. Description PrestaShop is an open-source e-commerce platform for creating and managing online stores. Its back-office Performance configuration includes a Debug mode for developers, which is enabled based on a specified cookie name and value. PrestaShop's debug-mode configuration code inserts the user-controlled values debug_cookie_name and debug_cookie_value into a PHP expression without adequately escaping or sanitizing them for use in PHP source code. The application writes this expression into the PHP define() statement in config/defines.inc.php or config/defines_custom.inc.php . A crafted value can terminate the intended string and introduce attacker-controlled PHP statements. The modified configuration file is loaded during application initialization, causing the injected code to execute on a subsequent request. Exploitation requires an authenticated back-office account with permission to modify debug mode settings and a configuration file writable by the PHP process. Root or operating-system administrator privileges are not required. Cross-site request forgery (CSRF) protection helps prevent unauthorized requests made through another user's session, but does not prevent exploitation by an attacker controlling an account with the required permissions. Injected code executes with the privileges of the PHP process. Affected release versions remain to be confirmed. Impact An authenticated attacker with the required configuration permissions could execute arbitrary PHP code in the security context of the PHP process. This could allow access to application secrets and customer data, modification or deletion of application files and database contents, and disruption of store operations. Operating-system command execution depends on the PHP configuration and available functions. The vulnerability does not independently grant root privileges. Solution PrestaShop version 9.2.1 addresses this vulnerability. Administrators should upgrade affected installations to version 9.2.1 or later. items.raw: Taiwanese vendor QNAP urges users to update Plex Media Server after reports of NAS compromises through the Plex2Shell vulnerability chain. QNAP urges users to update Plex Media Server through the QNAP App Center after reports that threat actors exploited the Plex2Shell vulnerability chain to compromise NAS devices. “QNAP has received reports from some users that Plex Media Server on their NAS appears to have been compromised through these vulnerabilities, and QNAP Technical Support is assisting the affected usersadvisory published by QNAP. ” reads the report published by the vendor. “The QNAP Product Security Incident Response Team (QNAP PSIRT) has confirmed that the vulnerabilities exist only in Plex Media Server; QTS, QuTS hero, and other QNAP operating systems are not themselves affected.” Plex Media Server is designed to make movies, music, and other media available across devices. But when a server is exposed to the internet and runs vulnerable software, it can become an entry point for attackers who have little interest in your film collection. On October 16, 2026, security researcher Zach Main published technical details and proof-of-concept (PoC) code for a vulnerability chain dubbed Plex2Shell. Within a day, researchers had observed attackers using the exploit against an internet-facing honeypot, deploying cryptocurrency-mining malware and proxy software. The incident is a reminder of how quickly a public exploit can be weaponized by threat actors. The chain combines four vulnerabilities in Plex Media Server: CVE-2026-96652, CVE-2026-96654, CVE-2026-96655, and CVE-2026-96656. Together, they can allow attackers to execute arbitrary code on vulnerable servers without valid credentials, provided the required conditions are met. The code runs with the privileges of the Plex service, giving attackers an opportunity to install additional software and abuse the host. The technical details are available in Main’s original analysis, Plex2Shell . Plex had been notified of the vulnerabilities on July 27 and acknowledged the report on August 4, awarding a bug bounty. The company released fixes in September, before the exploit code became public. The loader does not check the library’s name, executable permissions, digital signature, or symbols. items.title: Who Gives A Crap? Hackers, apparently, after toilet paper maker's customer data exposed
items.summary: UK shoppers caught up in third-party security mess, and nobody knows whether the data was flushed away
items.raw: Toilet paper purveyor Who Gives A Crap has found itself in a bit of a mess after an intruder accessed customer information through a third-party software provider, leaving the company scrambling to clean up a breach affecting shoppers in the UK, US, and Australia. In an email sent to affected customers over the weekend, seen by The Register, the loo roll seller warns that personal information was accessed without authorization after a security incident at an unnamed US-based marketing software provider. The email explains that the intruder gained access to the supplier's systems on October 30. The provider spotted the intrusion the following day and says it secured its systems by November 1, although Who Gives A Crap wasn't told until November 6. It's unclear why the supplier sat on the bad news for another five days before passing it on. The exposed information includes customers' names, email addresses, phone numbers, mailing addresses, and total spending with the company. In other words, someone may now know not only where you live, but just how much of your hard-earned cash you've flushed down the crapper. Payment information, order details, and passwords were not involved, and customers' accounts were not directly accessed. That's something of a relief, although whether the intruder actually made off with the data remains a pressing question. "We don't yet know whether the information was copied or downloaded," the company told customers, adding that it had found no evidence of misuse. In a separate public statement, Who Gives A Crap co-founder and CEO Simon Griffiths confirmed that the incident affected customers across the company's Australian, UK, and US stores. items.title: Outlook.com bounces legit emails as Microsoft's authentication crackdown goes sideways
items.summary: Missing DMARC or wobbly SPF means your mail may be treated as suspicious
items.raw: A validation error has stopped Outlook.com from accepting legitimate emails. The problem appears widespread and, according to reports from affected users, can result in non-delivery reports with error codes related to SPF (Sender Policy Framework) validation failures. Other users have reported errors highlighting a lack of DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance) information. The troubles began at the end of last week and appear to be the result of Microsoft tightening the rules (or at least attempting to do so) for accepting emails. The company's consumer email services are affected, and it appears that if a domain doesn't have working SPF or if it has a missing DMARC record, then Outlook.com and its ilk will treat it as suspicious and not accept emails. The rules are designed to deal with spam, bulk senders, and the like. In 2025, Microsoft announced new rules designed to strengthen email authentication for domains sending more than 5,000 emails per day. In addition to DMARC and SPF compliance, DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) was also required. Although this seemed like a good idea to ward off spammers, small senders now appear to be affected. According to complainants in the Outlook forum, a single email with just one line might now be rejected. Furthermore, Microsoft has not issued any advisory to customers explaining how the rules have changed. Although some customers insist their DMARC, SPF, and DKIM settings are compliant, many more have reported that once they set them to Microsoft's preferences, email began flowing once more. SPF must pass for the sending domain (the domain's DNS record should accurately list authorized IP addresses/hosts). DKIM must pass to validate email integrity and authenticity. DMARC must have at least p=none and align with either SPF or DKIM (preferably both). The Register asked the Windows giant for more information, but we have yet to receive a response. To make matters worse, the glitch also appears to be intermittent. A resend attempt might succeed following a rejection. To compound the situation, the rejection error message may also be vague about what caused the bounce in the first place. A moderator in Microsoft's support forum acknowledged the bug and said it was "classified as a service degradation." items.title: 13.3 million people’s medical data exposed; companies pay $300,000
items.summary: The New York AG reached a settlement with Perry Johnson & Associates and four related companies over a 2023 breach.
items.raw: The New York attorney general (AG) has reached a settlement over a medical data breach that affected 13.3 million people after basic security failures. Perry Johnson & Associates (PJ&A) and four related companies have agreed to pay $300,000 and implement extensive security reforms following a breach that exposed personal and medical information belonging to more than 13.3 million people. They face another $9.7 million in penalties if they fail to meet the settlement’s terms. New York AG Letitia James announced the agreement on November 6, alongside the attorneys general of Connecticut, Michigan, and New Jersey. Approximately 4.2 million of the people affected were New York residents. The investigation describes a series of failures: remote access without multifactor authentication , nearly identical passwords circulated by email, sensitive files without file-level encryption, and security software that detected malicious activity but did not alert security staff. The result: the companies only discovered the attack when the attackers contacted them on May 2, 2023, and demanded payment. How many people were affected? The stolen database files contained records associated with more than 13.3 million people, including approximately 4.2 million New Yorkers. Earlier reporting put the number of affected patients at approximately 8.95 million. The settlement documents now give the larger figure of more than 13.3 million. The total could be higher, since the AG found that attackers also accessed files in shared network storage containing personal and health information, but the companies did not review those files to identify additional affected people. The information included: Names, dates of birth, and home addresses. Social Security numbers. Medical record and hospital account numbers. Insurance information. Admission diagnoses and dates of treatment. Clinical information from medical transcriptions, including test results, medications, treatment facilities, and healthcare providers. See if your personal data has been exposed. SCAN NOW Notifications were also slow. PJ&A began contacting clients about the stolen database files in July 2023, and its clients notified affected individuals between October 31, 2023, and February 8, 2024. The New York AG found that the companies violated state requirements to disclose a breach as quickly as possible and without unreasonable delay. items.title: Japanese homeware giant pulls online store after cloud breach puts 7.7M records at risk

items.raw: Japanese electronics giant Iris Ohyama has taken down its online store after discovering that attackers may have accessed the personal information of 7.7 million customers, leaving shoppers unable to place orders. The retailer, which sells everything from home appliances and furniture to pet supplies, first disclosed the incident on October 29, a day after discovering a suspicious file on a third-party cloud service used by its Iris Plaza ecommerce operation. Iris Plaza immediately suspended its website and associated systems and began investigating, subsequently confirming unauthorized access. Iris Ohyama has since revealed that the potentially compromised cloud environment contained personal information belonging to approximately 5.8 million registered customers, including former members, and another 1.9 million people who had purchased products without creating an account or participated in promotional campaigns. The potentially exposed information includes names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, dates of birth, gender, and passwords, although the company says the exact information at risk varies between customers. Some of that data, including passwords, was encrypted, but Iris Ohyama hasn't explained what protection was used. It has advised customers who reused their Iris Plaza passwords elsewhere to change them, presumably before someone else gets the opportunity. There is some good news for anyone who has handed over their credit card details, as the retailer says it didn't store payment information in the affected cloud service and that it hasn't been compromised. It remains unclear whether the attackers actually made off with any personal information. In its FAQ, Iris Plaza says it is still investigating the possibility of a data leak and has yet to establish the full extent of the intrusion. Meanwhile, Iris Plaza's website is still down, and the company isn't saying when it'll be back. Orders are also taking longer to ship, while customers trying to cancel a purchase have been told they may have to turn the delivery driver away if their parcel arrives before the cancellation is processed. Fortunately for anyone desperate to buy a new rice cooker, Iris Plaza's stores on Rakuten, Yahoo! Shopping, and auPAY Market are still operating. The company says it has found no evidence that those stores were affected. items.raw: US agencies warn attackers are going after industrial refrigeration controllers. The fixes are basic, and most start with getting them off the internet. CISA, the FBI, HHS, USDA and the Department of Transportation published a joint advisory on attacks against industrial refrigeration controllers and cold chain monitoring systems. The activity is global. Healthcare, chemical, food and transport companies use these systems to watch temperatures, keep logs, run defrost cycles and save energy, including in refrigerated trucks. “The authoring organizations are aware of malicious cyber actors targeting electronic temperature controllers and commercial refrigeration controllers in retail grocery and cold storage facilities.” reads the advisory published by CISA. “The actors may exploit vulnerabilities or weaknesses in unpatched or internet-accessible controllers to remotely alter settings and force units into continuous heating and defrost cycles, which can cause widespread inventory loss and equipment hazards.” The targets are electronic temperature controllers and commercial refrigeration controllers used in grocery stores and cold-storage sites. Attackers may exploit flaws in unpatched or internet-accessible controllers to change settings remotely and force units into continuous heating and defrost cycles. In plain terms, someone could cook your freezer from the other side of the world. The agencies identify three ways in: bypassing authentication, injecting arbitrary code, and exploiting weak configurations. Once inside, an attacker can change temperatures, which can shorten equipment life, create a fire hazard and destroy stock. Spoiled products that reach consumers can also create a safety risk. “The actors may exploit vulnerabilities or weaknesses in unpatched or internet-accessible controllers to remotely alter settings and force units into continuous heating and defrost cycles, which can cause widespread inventory loss and equipment hazards.” continues the adviosry. An attacker can also hide the damage. Operators lose sight of current temperatures, and that’s a bad moment to learn a cold room has been warm for hours. CISA’s Chris Butera adds that every organization that depends on these systems should assume it’s a target. items.title: AI doesn’t have to go rogue to break the world
items.summary: AI systems are learning to exploit loopholes in everything from software to tax law. The biggest threat may not be malicious intent, but machines doing exactly what we ask.
items.raw: I want to talk about AI hacking. There are three aspects: people hacking AI systems, people using AI to hack other systems, and AIs hacking systems on their own, not even maliciously. The last two matter more than the first. The third is the weirdest and potentially the most destabilizing. I started writing about this in 2021 and in my 2022 book, A Hacker’s Mind . Back then I said it was mostly still science fiction, but not stupid science fiction. We’re seeing it more and more, especially in the past year. The trends I’m describing don’t require a major breakthrough in AI. They’re starting to happen now, and they’ll happen more often as AIs get better at autonomous problem-solving. And it will involve far more than computer code. AI will hack all sorts of social, economic and political systems. It will find vulnerabilities and exploit them. This is a difference in kind, not just degree. We’re not ready for it, and we need to think about the implications now. This article is adapted from a keynote speech delivered at the DEF CON 34 conference in Las Vegas on August 7, 2026. First, I want to broaden the term “hacking.” The tax code isn’t computer code, but it is code. It’s a series of algorithms with inputs and outputs. It has vulnerabilities, which we call loopholes, and exploits, which we call tax avoidance strategies. Black hat hackers exploit them for profit. We call them accountants and attorneys. What is a hack? One definition: “Something that a system permits, but is unanticipated and unwanted by the designers.” It’s subjective and implies novelty and cleverness. A hack follows the rules of a system but subverts its goals or intent, just as a software hack follows the logic of code while doing something its authors neither anticipated nor wanted. All systems of rules can be hacked, including professional sports, customer reward programs, financial systems and politics. Hacks even work against our cognitive functions. A curved hockey stick is a hack, and we know the name of the man who invented it. Mileage runs were a hack. The filibuster was originally a hack in Roman times. Gerrymandering is a hack. Hedge funds and private equity are full of them. A system is just a set of rules or norms, and the rules aren’t always formal. Even the best-designed rules will be incomplete, inconsistent or ambiguous. As long as people want to subvert a system’s goals, there will be hacks. AIs are becoming hackers. items.raw: In 1804, Napoleon gave France a code that much of the world still runs on. The Code civil replaced a tangle of local customs with a single written statute: orderly and knowable. In that tradition, the judge’s job, in Montesquieu’s phrase, is to be the mouth of the law, nothing more. Certainty was the point. Certainty has a cost. A codified system is only as current as its code. When the world produces something the code did not anticipate — a new technology, a new fraud — there is no statute to apply, and everyone waits for someone to write one. Your email security works exactly this way. That is the problem. Security by statute A signature is a statute. Someone observes an attack, writes a rule that describes it, and from that moment you are protected against that attack and its close relatives. It is fast, certain, and blind to anything the code has not been written to see. Signatures alone were never enough, so the industry made the code bigger. Anomaly detection and behavioral models are a thicker statute book, trained on what already happened and scoring how far a message deviates from it. More sophisticated than a signature, but not a different philosophy. A zero-day is a crime with no statute. The strongest evidence against codified defense is not the attack that fails a check. It is the attack that passes every one. When a supplier’s mailbox is compromised, the message arrives from a real domain, with valid credentials and earned reputation. Every check comes back clean because the infrastructure is genuine. Verizon’s 2026 Data Breach Investigations Report found that breaches involving a third party now account for 48% of the total, up 60% in a single year. Authentication did exactly what it measures : it confirmed the letter came from who it said, and had no rule for whether it should be believed. The code was consulted. The code said valid. The message was a theft in progress. Attackers understand this. A codified defense is cheap to walk around. You do not break the code; you do something it was never written to cover. The FBI’s 2025 Internet Crime Report put business email compromise losses above $3 billion in a single year, much of it carried by messages that broke no rule because no rule described them. items.title: Google DeepMind’s AI Agents Make 1024-Bit RSA Keys Cheaper to Attack
items.summary: Working with cryptographers, DeepMind’s AI agents cut the cost of forging RSA-1024 signatures and found a cheaper way to factor keys.

items.title: 7 dicas para alcançar a agilidade defensiva
items.summary: A agilidade na segurança defensiva reflete a capacidade de uma organização detetar, adaptar e responder rapidamente a ameaças cibernéticas sem perturbar as operações principais. Os especialistas apontam que as empresas devem abandonar arquiteturas estáticas em favor de iteração contínua, automação e flexibilidade. Como parte da estratégia, recomenda-se estabelecer uma base de zero-trust e modernizar a infraestrutura de segurança existente. O impacto destas medidas traduz-se numa melhoria da postura de risco e numa recuperação mais rápida de ataques inevitáveis.
points: Implementar uma abordagem zero-trust contínua em utilizadores e dispositivos.
Modernizar e racionalizar infraestruturas de segurança complexas e desatualizadas.
Utilizar sistemas baseados em IA para detetar e responder a ataques rapidamente.
items.title_original: 7 tips for achieving defensive agility
items.why: Permite às organizações adaptar-se a ameaças em evolução e minimizar disrupções no negócio.
items.todo: Integre o zero-trust nas operações diárias e avalie a infraestrutura de segurança existente.

items.title: Ferramentas falsas de segurança do GitHub infetam mais de 2.000 PCs com malware
items.summary: Uma campanha de malware tem utilizado o GitHub para distribuir ferramentas falsas de segurança direcionadas a entusiastas de jogos blockchain e profissionais de cibersegurança. Mais de 2.000 computadores foram infetados através de projetos comprometidos que continham scripts maliciosos. O malware recolhe informações do sistema, desativa o Windows Defender e remove vários produtos antivírus conhecidos. O impacto afeta diretamente os utilizadores infetados, cujos dados confidenciais e sistemas ficam expostos aos atacantes.
points: Atacantes ocultaram malware em projetos do GitHub simulando ferramentas de segurança.
A campanha infetou mais de 2.000 PCs de fãs de jogos e profissionais de TI.
O malware desativa o Windows Defender e desinstala antivírus como McAfee e ESET.
Scripts do PowerShell descarregam componentes que roubam dados e comunicam com bots do Telegram.
items.title_original: Fake GitHub Security Tools Infect Over 2,000 PCs With Malware
items.why: Compromete dados sensíveis e desativa defesas críticas de milhares de sistemas.
items.todo: Verifique a autenticidade das ferramentas de segurança descarregadas e mantenha os antivírus atualizados.

items.title: Uma semana em segurança (2 de novembro – 8 de novembro)
items.summary: O panorama semanal da cibersegurança destacou múltiplos incidentes e vulnerabilidades a afetar empresas e utilizadores globais. Entre os casos encontram-se falhas críticas corrigidas em navegadores, ataques a sistemas de armazenamento de sangue e superfícies de televisão inteligente a ignorar definições de privacidade. Verificaram-se também incidentes em cadeias de retalho e compromissos em plataformas de jogos. O impacto abrange a exposição de dados de milhões de utilizadores e riscos operacionais graves.
points: O Google Chrome corrigiu 213 falhas de segurança, incluindo 7 críticas.
Uma violação num cartão de crédito da Revolve afetou cerca de 1,5 milhões de pessoas.
Ataques a sistemas de refrigeração e sangue alarmaram as autoridades norte-americanas.
items.title_original: A week in security (November 2 – November 8)
items.why: Resume os principais riscos e incidentes que marcaram a semana no setor tecnológico.
items.todo: Atualize regularmente o software e monitorize os dados pessoais contra potenciais fugas.

items.title: Antigo engenheiro da OpenAI declara-se não culpado de colocar dispositivo oculto em sala de reuniões executiva
items.summary: O antigo engenheiro da OpenAI, Abdulrahman Alfozan, declarou-se não culpado perante um tribunal federal de São Francisco das acusações de colocar um dispositivo de gravação de áudio oculto num escritório da empresa. O caso, revelado no mês passado, levou à detenção do cidadão saudita. O impacto centra-se nas implicações legais e na segurança interna da empresa de inteligência artificial.
points: O engenheiro Abdulrahman Alfozan foi acusado de plantar um gravador de áudio num escritório.
O suspeito declarou-se não culpado num tribunal federal em São Francisco.
A próxima audiência do caso foi agendada para novembro de 2026.
items.title_original: Former OpenAI Engineer Pleads Not Guilty to Planting Covert Device in Executive Meeting Room
items.why: Evidencia potenciais falhas de segurança física e espionagem interna em empresas tecnológicas de topo.
items.todo: Reforce os controlos de acesso físico e a monitorização de áreas sensíveis nas instalações.

items.title: A BBC tem um plano para um evento Black Sky, e funciona através de rádio FM
items.summary: A BBC desenvolveu um plano de emergência baseado em rádio FM para manter a população britânica informada durante apagões prolongados e falhas totais de infraestruturas. A estratégia baseia-se em lições retiradas de inundações anteriores, onde a dependência excessiva de infraestruturas digitais deixou comunidades sem comunicações vitais. O impacto de um evento Black Sky envolveria a falha simultânea de eletricidade, água e comunicações, tornando o rádio FM num meio essencial de sobrevivência informativa.
points: A BBC preparou estúdios auto-suficientes para emitir rádio FM durante 72 horas em caso de apagão.
Incidentes passados mostraram a vulnerabilidade das sociedades dependentes de infraestruturas digitais.
O plano visa mitigar os riscos de um evento Black Sky que interrompa eletricidade e comunicações.
items.title_original: The BBC has a plan for a Black Sky event, and it runs on FM radio
items.why: Garante o acesso a informações essenciais à população quando a infraestrutura digital colapsa.
items.todo: Tenha sempre um rádio a pilhas ou dínamo acessível para receber avisos em caso de emergência prolongada.

items.title: Agências dos EUA alertam que ataques a controladores de refrigeração podem causar incêndios e perdas de inventário
items.summary: Agências governamentais dos Estados Unidos emitiram um alerta global sobre ataques direcionados a sistemas industriais de refrigeração e monitorização da cadeia de frio. Os atacantes exploram vulnerabilidades em controladores acessíveis através da internet para alterar remotamente definições e forçar o aquecimento contínuo das unidades. O impacto destes ataques inclui graves interrupções de serviço, perigos de incêndio e perda total de inventário armazenado.
points: Atores maliciosos visam sistemas industriais de refrigeração e monitorização a nível global.
As explorações ocorrem em controladores sem patches ou acessíveis diretamente pela internet.
Os ataques podem provocar alterações térmicas forçadas, incêndios e perda de inventário.
items.title_original: U.S. Agencies Warn Refrigeration Controller Attacks Could Cause Fires and Inventory Losses
items.why: Protege infraestruturas críticas e cadeias de abastecimento contra danos físicos e materiais severos.
items.todo: Assegure que os controladores industriais não estão diretamente expostos à internet e aplique as atualizações de segurança necessárias.
